0.0.n: お adds politeness to 店; here it refers to the restaurant.

0.1.n: Links the restaurant to its people, forming an expression for the staff.

0.2.n: 人 means person or people; お店の人 refers to people working at the restaurant.

0.3.n: Adds the staff to the ongoing discussion; English may leave this unstated.

0.4.n: Sets the timing at the beginning of the restaurant visit.

0.6.n: お冷 is a restaurant term for cold water served to customers.

0.7.n: Joins the water and the hand towel as items brought together.

0.8.n: This is an incomplete piece of おしぼり, not a separate word here.

0.9.n: Together with おし, this forms おしぼり; the supplied ぼる label does not apply here.

0.10.n: Marks the water and towel as the things the staff bring.

0.11.n: 持つ in its て-form joins くる, expressing carrying something toward the speaker or customer.

0.12.n: The preceding verb describes what happens at this time.

0.13.n: Marks 時 as the time when the staff say the following words.

1.1.n: ご makes 注文 polite, showing respect for the customer's order.

1.2.n: Marks the order as what becomes decided.

1.3.n: お plus the stem of 決まる forms part of the respectful expression お決まりになる.

1.4.n: Connects お決まり to なる in a pattern that respectfully describes the customer's action.

1.5.n: なる becomes なりましたら, a polite conditional form; the full expression respectfully refers to the customer deciding.

2.0.n: Refers to the table bell customers use to summon staff.

2.1.n: Marks the bell as the tool used to call the staff.

2.2.n: お plus the stem of 呼ぶ pairs with ください to make a respectful request.

2.3.n: Completes お呼びください, politely asking the customer to call the staff.

2.5.n: Introduces the quoted wording as an example of what the staff say.

2.6.n: ふう refers to the manner of speaking shown by the quotation.

2.7.n: Makes というふう describe how the staff speak.

2.8.n: The polite form of 言う describes what staff typically say.

3.0.n: Points to the phrase just quoted and directly modifies フレーズ.

3.1.n: This borrowed word refers to the restaurant expression just introduced.

3.2.n: Makes this phrase the topic; it is the thing you will hear.

3.3.n: Emphasizes the speaker's certainty that listeners will encounter the phrase.

3.4.n: The polite form of 聞く refers here to hearing the phrase on a future visit.

3.5.n: Adds emphasis, presenting the information confidently to the listener.

4.1.n: ご adds respect when referring to the customer's order.

4.2.n: Marks the order as what becomes decided.

4.3.n: お plus the stem of 決まる is part of the respectful pattern お決まりになる.

4.4.n: Connects お決まり to なる, completing a pattern used to show respect for the customer.

4.5.n: なりましたら is the polite conditional form of なる, introducing when the customer should call.

4.7.n: Refers to the table bell used to get the staff's attention.

4.8.n: Identifies the bell as the tool for calling the staff.

4.9.n: お plus the stem of 呼ぶ begins a respectful request completed by ください.

4.10.n: Completes the polite request お呼びください, directed at the customer.

5.0.n: Casual speech uses すごい to strengthen an adjective where more standard wording would use すごく.

5.1.n: Describes how widely recognized the phrase is and needs な before a noun.

5.2.n: Connects 有名 to フレーズ so that it describes the phrase.

5.3.n: Refers again to the quoted restaurant expression.

5.4.n: The linking form of だ connects this description to the next statement.

6.0.n: 日本 is the country name, used here as the destination of a visit.

6.1.n: Marks Japan as the destination of 行く.

6.2.n: The past form of 行く combines with ことがある to describe a past experience.

6.3.n: Turns 行った into an experience that can be described with がある.

6.4.n: Marks the experience expressed by こと as what exists in the pattern ことがある.

6.5.n: Completes 行ったことがある, describing people who have been to Japan at least once.

6.6.n: The entire preceding expression describes which people the speaker means.

6.7.n: Makes people who have visited Japan the topic of the sentence.

6.9.n: Strongly emphasizes the claim that those visitors have heard the phrase.

6.10.n: The past form of 聞く combines with ことがあります to express previous experience.

6.11.n: Turns 聞いた into an experience rather than referring to one specific occasion.

6.12.n: Marks the hearing experience as what exists in the pattern ことがあります.

6.13.n: The polite form of ある completes 聞いたことがあります, saying someone has heard it before.

0.lit: The shop's people also, at first, when bringing water and a hand towel,
0.tip: A verb followed by 時に means when that action happens.

1.lit: Once your order has been decided,
1.tip: お決まりになりましたら is a respectful way to say once you have decided.

2.lit: Please call us using the bell, they say in that way.
2.tip: お plus a verb stem plus ください forms a respectful request.

3.lit: As for this phrase, you will definitely hear it, I assure you.
3.tip: よ adds confident emphasis when giving the listener information.

4.lit: Once your order has been decided, please call us using the bell.
4.tip: で marks the bell as the tool used to call the staff.

5.lit: It is a very well-known phrase, and,
5.tip: The final で links this description to the next sentence instead of ending it.

6.lit: As for people who have experienced going to Japan, they definitely have experienced hearing it.
6.tip: A past-form verb plus ことがある means having done something before.
